summary: Once an open repair is past its recorded target, send it to the facilities duty lead for review. An existing escalation stays on the job.

clarification_question: Does any other fixed light work in that same room?
summary: For fixed room lighting, use P3 with a seven-day target if another fixed light works in the same room. If no fixed light works, use P2 with a 24-hour repair target from the first confirmation. Portable lights and lighting in other rooms do not count. Ask if the state of other fixed lights is unclear. Dark shared escape routes need urgent assessment.
Create a heating repair proposal with a two-day target for a verified heating fault. Suspected gas or carbon monoxide hazards go to manual review.
Create an appliance repair proposal with a seven-day target for a verified appliance fault. Suspected hazards go to manual review.

An active lockout requires urgent contact with on-duty residence staff. Staff help restore access as soon as possible after checking identity and access rights. A spare or replacement key is routine if access is available. Treat an identifiable lost or stolen key or a door that will not secure or open from inside as urgent. Ask whether the resident can get in now if unclear.
lockout_reply: Contact residence reception or the on-duty residence staff now. Use your residence’s published out-of-hours contact if reception is closed. Staff can help you regain access as soon as possible after checking your identity and access rights.

summary: Route any urgent issue immediately. Keep the original report and let the reviewer separate the remaining issues at the verified location for their own triage. Each issue gets its own review.

Use the same verified location and fitting to identify an existing open job. Surface its job number, existing target and the resident’s new evidence for review. Reassess urgency based on the current condition and block a duplicate repair.

Give urgent staff handling to uncontrolled or spreading water, ceiling leaks, total power loss, electrical hazards (including water reaching electrical fittings), unsafe shared routes, broken glass on a shared route, structural collapse and lift entrapment. Match the current condition before routine triage, even when an open job already exists. A single dead socket without hazard signs needs ordinary review. Ask about scope if unclear.

clarification_question: Is the tap or shower only dripping, or is water spreading beyond the fitting?
summary: A contained tap or shower drip without hazard signs has a P3 fourteen-day target. Ask one question if the extent is unclear. Water spreading outside the fitting, uncontrolled water or water coming through a ceiling requires urgent human assessment.
If you’re dissatisfied with how an unresolved maintenance issue was handled, you can contact your building manager to raise a complaint.

Ask one targeted question when a missing fact changes the route. If it cannot be confirmed, or the report is contradictory, unsupported or could not be interpreted, send it to the residence duty reviewer with the original report and reason. Hold any repair action for staff review.

Active fire, smoke from a possible fire, or a sounding fire alarm with no confirmed drill requires emergency handling. A faulty detector, chirping alarm, obstructed escape route, or defective fire door without an active incident requires urgent residence staff assessment.
reply: If you see fire or smoke, or a fire alarm is sounding and staff have not confirmed a drill, call 999 immediately. Follow your building’s fire instructions and the emergency operator’s directions. If you cannot get out safely, tell the operator exactly where you are.

summary: Suspected gas leak, smell of gas, or a carbon monoxide alarm requires emergency handling. A heating fault with no sign of gas or carbon monoxide follows the heating policy.
reply: Call the National Gas Emergency Service immediately on 0800 111 999 from a safe place. If anyone is in immediate danger, call 999.
